questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook traditional Italian dishes like lasagne at home
Why tourists love visiting Italy
How Italian neighbourhoods abroad spread Italian food
The most popular Italian food in Britain
questions.why: They take a walk through two Little Italys, in Argentina and New York.

questions.q: Why does Georgie describe cafes selling mozzarella and focaccia?
options: To see if Neil can guess where she is
To recommend a café in London
To explain how to make fresh focaccia at home
To say she is hungry
questions.why: She asks, “Where would I be then?” after describing the Italian food.

questions.q: How did Italian food become famous around the world?
options: Italian chefs went on TV
Local people started eating immigrants' food too
The Italian government advertised it
Tourists brought Italian recipes home from their holidays
questions.why: Neil says shops and cafes served their communities, then dishes attracted local people.

questions.q: What do we learn about Hugo Banchero's grandfather, Giuseppe?
options: He was born in Buenos Aires
He moved to New York first
He opened a small food shop in Manhattan, New York
He arrived from Genoa as a young child
questions.why: Hugo says he came from Genoa and arrived at the age of seven and a half.

questions.q: What is faina, according to Hugo?
options: A pizza made with chickpea flour
A kind of Italian cheese
A sweet pastry
A pasta dish served with meatballs
questions.why: He says faina from Genoa is a pizza with chickpea flour.

questions.q: What is special about Little Italy in New York?
options: It was designed and built by the De Palo family in 1925
It is the newest Little Italy
Most Italian immigrants to the US came through it
It only sells pizza
questions.why: Georgie says 90% of Italian immigrants to the US at the turn of the century came through it.

questions.q: How has the De Palo family business changed, according to Lou?
options: It has moved to another city
It now only sells food from one region, Liguria
It is run by a new family
It now sells food from all 20 regions of Italy
questions.why: He says the business expanded to represent the food culture of the 20 regions of Italy.

questions.q: Why does Lou call Little Italy a “stepping stone”?
options: Its streets are made of stone
Immigrants lived there first, then moved on
It is next to a river
It was the first step in building New York City
questions.why: Italians first settled there, then eventually moved into mainstream America.
